_note: Maintained by hand in the GitHub editor. THREE steps per report cycle: (1) before the report, fill each analyst's `value` and a `source` link for the metrics they publicly posted, and the `consensus` (trade average) per metric; (2) after USDA releases, fill each metric's `actual`; (3) the build script scores everyone automatically. Only keep analysts whose numbers you can source from a public post/interview/survey — leave a value null if you don't have it. Never invent a number. Add a new block under `reports` for each future report.

metrics.label: 2026/27 corn yield

estimates.source_note: Current conditions-yield model nowcast (ratings week ending 2026-08-09), locked 2026-08-11 pre-report in the direction ledger (data/nowcast-direction.json). Supersedes the retired ge-linear-v1 call (corn 189.4 / beans 56.2, locked 2026-07-25) — the supersession is on the record in git history.
StoneX customer survey, published Aug 5-6 2026; Arlan Suderman on the record calling it "a trend yield corn crop." Same interview gave Iowa 218, Illinois 212.

Jerry Gulke, AgWeb Aug 7 2026: corn "could be closer to 180.5 to 181 bu. per acre." He stated a RANGE, not a point — 180.75 is the midpoint, used only so the call can be scored. Set to null to drop it.

metrics.consensus_note: Average of private pre-report estimates published ahead of the Aug 12 WASDE (AgWeb, Aug 7 2026). No low/high was published for the poll, so no range is claimed.

metrics.label: 2026/27 corn yield
metrics.consensus_note: Dow Jones pre-report survey, reported by DTN on 2026-09-09: "For Friday, the average trade guess is calling for a 178.1 bpa yield." The high and low are the survey's own, from the same table (182.9 / 173.2). Typed from the published survey, never computed here.

estimates.source_note: Pro Farmer's 2026 crop tour national corn estimate, published at the end of tour week and already carried in data/crop-tour.json. It is the low end of the Dow Jones survey range, which is why 173.2 appears in both places.

metrics.label: 2026/27 soybean yield
metrics.consensus_note: Dow Jones pre-report survey, reported by DTN on 2026-09-09: analysts expect "another slight cut to the national soybean yield, with an average trade guess of 52.5 bpa." High and low (53.3 / 51.5) are from the same survey table. NO PRO FARMER CALL IS FILED HERE. A secondary write-up attributed 53.3 bu/acre to the tour, but Pro Farmer publishes soybeans as production (4.572 bb), not a yield -- data/crop-tour.json says so in measure_note: "Tour soybean numbers are pod counts in a 3x3 foot square, not a yield." 53.3 is the survey high, and whoever's arithmetic it is, it is not Pro Farmer's published number.

metrics.label: 2026/27 corn ending stocks
metrics.consensus_note: Dow Jones pre-report survey, reported by DTN on 2026-09-09: corn ending stocks cut 120 mb to 1.533 bb (the same survey and figure data/wpi-estimates.json carries). No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so no range is claimed and it is graded on the 2% band. Actual 1.567 bb from USDA's September WASDE, reported by DTN on 2026-09-11 (https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/article/2026/09/11/usda-releases-september-crop-wasde-2).

metrics.label: 2026/27 soybean ending stocks
metrics.consensus_note: Dow Jones pre-report survey, reported by DTN on 2026-09-09: soybean ending stocks cut 30 mb to 290 mb. Reuters' survey averaged 298 mb; the Dow Jones figure is used because it is the survey every other September figure here is graded against, and 310 is above both. No survey low or high is on file for this figure, so no range is claimed and it is graded on the 2% band. Actual 310 mb from USDA's September WASDE, reported by DTN on 2026-09-11 (https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/ag/news/article/2026/09/11/usda-releases-september-crop-wasde-2).

metrics.label: Wheat stocks, all positions, Sept 1
metrics.consensus_note: The only pre-report survey found (Pro Farmer, 2026-09-26) printed a wheat trade average (1.889 billion bushels) next to a cited WASDE figure that does not read as a comparable wheat ending-stocks number, and the two could not be reconciled against USDA's own current estimate. Left blank rather than publish a number that might not measure what it claims to.
